# IngrediLens

> IngrediLens is an iPhone and iPad app that reads the ingredient list on food and cosmetic labels and highlights the allergens and ingredients you chose to avoid, including “may contain” warnings. It reads labels in English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French and Italian, works without an account, and keeps your data on your device. It is free to download, with an optional Premium subscription.

Key facts: iPhone and iPad (iOS / iPadOS 17+). Free download with 2 filters; optional Premium subscription (monthly with 3-day free trial, yearly with 7-day free trial). No account; data stays on the device; no ads or tracking. Reads labels in English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French and Italian; free restaurant allergy card in 15 languages. Built-in database of more than 24,000 ingredients with cited sources (EU Regulations 1169/2011, 1223/2009, 1333/2008, CosIng, US FDA FALCPA/FASTER Act). Not a medical device: it never says a product is safe, cannot detect cross-contact, and users must always read the pack. Developer: Enescan İşler (independent). Current version 1.4 (28 October 2026). Contact: enescanisler@icloud.com

- About / fact page (canonical facts, method, sources): https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/about/

## Guides (English)

- [All guides (hub)](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/): food allergy and label guides in English, Español, Português, Deutsch, Français, Italiano
- [How to read allergen labels on food (EU, UK and US)](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/how-to-read-allergen-labels/): In the EU and UK, allergens are part of the ingredients list and must be emphasised, usually in bold.
- [What does "may contain" mean on food labels?](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/may-contain-traces-meaning/): “May contain” and “traces of” warn about possible cross-contact: the allergen is not in the recipe but could get into the product during production.
- [The 14 EU allergens list, explained with examples](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/eu-14-allergens-list/): EU and UK law (Annex II of Regulation 1169/2011) lists 14 allergens that must be emphasised in the ingredients list: cereals containing gluten, crustaceans, eggs, fish, peanuts, soybeans, milk, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites, lupin and molluscs.
- [The 9 major food allergens in the US (FALCPA and sesame)](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/us-major-food-allergens/): US food labels must declare nine major allergens: milk, egg, fish, crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soybeans and sesame, which was added from 1 January 2023 by the FASTER Act.
- [E-numbers explained, what the codes on food labels mean](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/e-numbers-explained/): E-numbers are codes for food additives authorised in the EU, such as E330 for citric acid; the label shows the additive’s function followed by its name or E-number.
- [Hidden gluten on food labels, names to look for](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/hidden-gluten-names/): Gluten is in wheat (including spelt, durum, semolina and khorasan), barley, rye and foods made from them, such as malt, bulgur, couscous and seitan.
- [Hidden milk on labels, other names for dairy](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/hidden-milk-names/): Milk can appear as casein, caseinates, whey, lactose, ghee, butter, cream, curd or milk solids.
- [Hidden egg on food labels, other names for egg](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/hidden-egg-names/): Egg can appear on labels as albumen or albumin, ovalbumin, ovomucoid, lysozyme (E1105), egg lecithin or dried egg.
- [Hidden soy on food labels, other names for soya](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/hidden-soy-names/): Soy can appear as soya, soy lecithin (E322), edamame, miso, tempeh, tofu, textured vegetable protein (TVP) or hydrolysed soy protein, and on cosmetics as Glycine Soja.
- [Hidden peanut and tree nut names on food labels](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/hidden-peanut-tree-nut-names/): Peanuts are legumes and tree nuts are a separate allergen group, so labels and allergists treat them separately.
- [Sesame, mustard, celery and lupin, the overlooked allergens](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/sesame-mustard-celery-lupin/): Sesame, mustard, celery and lupin are on the EU’s list of 14 allergens and often hide in tahini, spice mixes, stock cubes, sauces and gluten-free flours.
- [Travelling with food allergies, restaurant allergy cards](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/restaurant-allergy-card-travel/): Before a trip with a food allergy, update your plan with your doctor, pack your adrenaline auto-injectors and learn the local words for your allergens and “may contain”.
- [Eating out with coeliac disease, a practical guide](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/eating-out-coeliac-disease/): With coeliac disease even small amounts of gluten matter, so eating out depends on how the kitchen avoids cross-contamination.
- [Food allergies at school and childcare, what to give carers](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/food-allergy-school-plan/): Give the school, nursery or carer an allergy action plan completed with your child’s doctor, in-date adrenaline auto-injectors if prescribed, and a clear list of the foods to avoid with their other names.
- [Reading cosmetic INCI ingredient lists for sensitive skin](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/cosmetic-ingredients-sensitive-skin/): Cosmetic ingredients are listed by INCI name in descending order of amount, with ingredients under 1% in any order at the end.
- [How to choose an allergen scanner app, a checklist](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/allergen-scanner-app-checklist/): Allergen scanner apps either look up a barcode in a database or read the ingredient list printed on the pack.
- [How to keep a food reaction diary to find triggers](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/food-reaction-diary/): A reaction diary records what you ate or used, when symptoms started, what they were and how bad they were, plus foods you tolerated.
- [Allergy and ingredient scanner apps compared](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/allergy-scanner-apps-compared/): Scanner apps fall into four groups: barcode scorers (such as Yuka), diet and allergy filters (such as Fig), cosmetic ingredient apps (such as INCI Beauty and Think Dirty) and label readers (such as IngrediLens).
- [IngrediLens: questions and answers](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/ingredilens-faq/): IngrediLens reads food and cosmetic ingredient lists with the iPhone camera, a photo, typed text or a barcode, and highlights the allergens you choose plus "may contain" statements.
- [Yuka alternative for food allergies: what to use](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/guides/en/yuka-alternative-food-allergies/): Yuka rates the overall health impact of food and cosmetics, which is useful for healthier shopping.

## Free tools

- [Free restaurant allergy card (15 languages)](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/allergy-card/): Make, print or save a card that explains your food allergies to restaurant staff abroad.
- [Ingredient list allergen checker](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/ingredient-checker/): Paste an ingredient list and see which of your allergens and “may contain” warnings it mentions.
- Allergy card in other languages: [Español](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/es/tarjeta-de-alergias/), [Português](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/pt/cartao-de-alergia/), [Deutsch](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/de/allergiekarte/), [Français](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/fr/carte-allergies/), [Italiano](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/it/scheda-allergie/)
- Ingredient checker in other languages: [Español](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/es/comprobar-ingredientes/), [Português](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/pt/verificar-ingredientes/), [Deutsch](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/de/zutatenliste-pruefen/), [Français](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/fr/verifier-ingredients/), [Italiano](https://isler404.github.io/apps/ingredilens/it/controllo-ingredienti/)
